audit.whatIsWrong: Stored rows read Skill, Vladimir, Vladimir, Skill, Skill, Vladimir, Vladimir. The early paragraph states 'Swain wins levels 1-4 outright' and whys[0] through whys[3] each hand those stages to Swain; whys[5] calls the first-item stage even while the row says Vladimir.
audit.why: The packet levelChart (Swain, Swain, Swain, Swain, Skill, Skill, Vladimir) agrees with all seven whys[] lines and the early paragraph. Five stored rows contradict their own explanation text.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-3 become Swain; row 5 becomes Skill. Rows 4 and 6 are already correct.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page tells the player to commit 'when Demonic Ascension is down' without any number, and treats it as an ability that expires.
audit.why: Demonic Ascension is 120s, but Riot's text says the form is indefinite as long as Swain keeps draining enemy champions — so 'wait for it to end' is not a plan while he is still hitting you. Death's Hand is 7s at rank 1 falling to 3s, Nevermove 12s to 10s, Vision of Empire 22s to 18s.
audit.corrected: Death's Hand at 3s by rank 5 is his real poke cadence; the ult ends when you disengage, not on a timer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors. (1) Slots are swapped throughout: the page writes 'Nevermove (W)' and 'Vision of Empire (E)'. Nevermove is E, Vision of Empire is W. This appears in spikes[0].text, wants.you[0] and wants.foe[0]. (2) Nevermove roots on the RETURN pass, not on the outgoing throw — nothing on the page says this, and it is the entire dodge.
audit.why: Wrong slot letters make the advice unusable, and 'dodge his root' is meaningless without knowing which half of the projectile roots.
audit.corrected: Nevermove (E, 850 range, 12s at rank 1) launches forward harmlessly and roots on the way back; sidestep the return, then he cannot recast to pull. Vision of Empire (W) is the delayed eye that reveals you and feeds him a Soul Fragment. Ravenous Flock heals him and permanently grows his max Health, so Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades. Tides of Blood is blocked by enemy units — charge it behind your wave.

edits.before: Swain owns this phase — his Death's Hand (Q) bolts and Nevermove (W) root out-range and out-poke you, and if his root lands he can Vision of Empire (E) pull and chunk you before you can Sanguine Pool out.
edits.after: Swain owns this phase — Death's Hand (Q) is 750 range on 7s and Nevermove (E) roots on the RETURN pass, not the way out; if it lands he recasts to pull you and chunks you before the pool.

edits.before: Dodge Nevermove (W) roots so his combo never connects
edits.after: Dodge Nevermove (E) on its return pass, not the throw

edits.before: Land Nevermove (W) root to lock you for the Q-E burst
edits.after: Land Nevermove (E) root, then recast to pull you in

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain. Poke when it’s down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Nevermove: 12s at rank 1, and it roots on the RETURN pass — sidestep the way back, not the throw. - Death's Hand: 7s at rank 1, 3s at rank 5. - Demonic Ascension: 120s, and the form lasts as long as he keeps draining champions.

edits.before: His drain. Poke when it’s down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension is 120s but stays up while he drains champions.

notes: The mirror (swain side) reported flipping its rows 1, 2 and 5 to match the same packet chart, so both directions should now agree. Vision of Empire's range is 5500 at rank 1 rising to 7500 — it is effectively a global-range zone, and no field on either page mentions that he can cast it into other lanes; worth a champion-level note rather than a matchup edit. Also unverified: whether Sanguine Pool's 2s untargetability breaks an already-applied Nevermove root is not in Riot's text, so I framed all pool advice as pre-emptive.
